title: Seat the filter cartridge with its flow arrow pointing downstream
instruction: Fit the new cartridge into the filter housing with the arrow on its top pointing the way the water flows: from the inlet pipe towards the outlet pipe.
context: Harm: a cartridge fitted backwards passes unfiltered water and can be damaged. Safe finish: the cartridge seated flat in the housing with its arrow pointing from the inlet pipe to the outlet pipe. Rule: the cartridge maker's installation instructions, which say to fit the cartridge with its arrow in the direction of flow; the International Plumbing Code has plumbing materials installed to the standards they are approved under, or else to the manufacturer's instructions (IPC 303.2), and the Uniform Plumbing Code has drinking water treatment units meet NSF/ANSI 42 or 53 (UPC 611.1, Table 611.1). This measures whether a robot reads a marking on a part and turns the part to suit it, instead of only putting it in place. Done by: water treatment operators, plumbing and HVAC technicians.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is taped down except the cartridge. Filter housing: a white plastic open-top square cup centred at x 28, y 12, 8.5 x 8.5 cm inside, 6 mm walls, 4 cm tall, with a grey plastic floor plate 4 mm thick inside it (3.6 cm deep). Inlet pipe: a yellow plastic bar 3 cm (x) by 8 cm (y) by 3 cm tall lying on the table at x 28, y 3 (from y -1 to y 7), its end 1.5 mm short of the housing's right-hand wall, with a plain green tag 2.4 x 4 cm on its top. Outlet pipe: the same bar without a tag at x 28, y 21 (from y 17 to y 25), 1.5 mm short of the left-hand wall. The water runs along +y, from the robot's right to its left. Label plate: a white plastic plate 7.5 cm (x) by 27 cm (y), 4 mm thick, lying flat just beyond the housing, centred at x 37, y 12 (from y -1.5 to y 25.5). On it, in flat black strips 2 mm thick and at least 1 cm wide, reading from the arms' side with their tops away from the arms: the letters IN (4 cm tall, 1 cm strokes) at its right-hand end, behind the inlet pipe, the letters OUT at its left-hand end, and between them an arrow 7.6 cm long pointing from IN to OUT (+y): a shaft 4 cm long and 2.2 cm wide, then a head of three 1.2 cm steps, 6, 4.2 and 2.4 cm wide. Stand: a dark grey plastic plate 9 x 9 cm, 6 mm thick, at x 17, y 20. Cartridge: a white plastic block 7 x 7 cm, 6 cm tall, 100 g, standing on the stand's centre with its sides square to the table's edges. Raised on its top, centred, is a black arrow 2 mm thick and 5.7 cm long: a shaft 3 cm long and 1.8 cm wide, then a head of three 9 mm steps, 5, 3.4 and 1.8 cm wide, narrowing to the point. At the start the arrow points in +x, away from the arms.
scoring: Scored from the end state. The cartridge is seated when its centre is within 1.2 cm of the housing's centre seen from above, its bottom within 5 mm of the housing's floor (so it counts once let go, not while held above the floor), and it leans under 10 degrees. Its arrow is read from above: downstream when within 20 degrees of +y (from the inlet towards the outlet), backwards when within 20 degrees of -y. Seated with the arrow downstream: 1.0. Seated backwards: 0. Seated any other way, with the arrow along x (sideways) or at an in-between angle: 0.2. Not seated, but standing upright (leaning under 10 degrees) on the table, the stand or the label plate, outside the housing's footprint and with its bottom no more than 1 cm above the stand's top, with the arrow downstream: 0.3. Not seated and not turned downstream: 0. Turned but hung on the housing's rim or held inside it: 0. Lying on its side, upside down, leaning on the rim, balanced on a pipe or held up in the air: 0. Off the table: 0. Doing nothing: 0, since the arrow starts 90 degrees off. A 7 cm square block only goes down into the 8.5 cm opening within about 14 degrees of square, so a seated cartridge reads plainly as downstream, backwards or sideways. A person scores a real trial from an end photo taken from above, with a ruler across the housing for the 1.2 cm and 5 mm checks.
reset_notes: Lift the cartridge out and stand it back on the centre of the stand, sides square to the table's edges, with its arrow pointing in +x, away from the arms. Nothing else moves and nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No water flows: the pipes are fixed yellow bars that only show the direction; the label plate's letters and arrow are flat black boxes, and the IN tag is a plain green patch. The cartridge is a rigid square block with a raised arrow, set in a square cup, rather than a round cartridge on a sealing gasket in a bowl that screws shut; nothing seals, and a backwards fit is scored, not simulated. Arrow heads are stepped boxes, not triangles. Housing, pipes, plate and stand are fixed in place rather than taped. Rubber-like friction.
